extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, economists, and patent scholars conducting empirical analyses of patent prosecution and standard-essential patents (SEPs)
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical evaluation of how standard publication affects continuation and child-application filing behavior for standard-essential patents (SEPs) relative to matched control patent applications using DiD and event-study methods and multiple robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of SEP (primary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A SEP is the earliest U.S. utility patent application of a domestic patent family that contains at least one U.S. utility patent application declared essential for a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the main SEP definition used in the analysis; an alternative, narrower SEP definition (used in robustness checks) includes only patents and patent applications explicitly mentioned in SSO disclosure letters (i.e., excluding undeclared U.S. family members of declared SEPs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of control application
rubrics_metrics.description: A control application is the earliest U.S. utility patent application of a domestic patent family that does not contain any U.S. utility patent applications declared essential for a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls are typically drawn from the same technology centers and matched on observable characteristics (see matching criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample inclusion and time-at-risk rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is included in the sample from its filing quarter to the latest disposal quarter of an application in its U.S. patent family, or the end of year 2016 if its family is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a robustness check, the authors alternatively define time-at-risk using only the focal application's pendency (discarding pendency of its children) and for controls use the pendency of the earliest filing of each non-SEP family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching criteria for matched controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Match SEPs and controls on art unit, examiner, and filing year (for some analyses match on art-unit-examiner-filing-quarter groups); in some specifications match on filing month and technology center or on pre-standard continuation counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-to-one matching is used (without replacement), breaking ties at random; alternative matched samples include matching on cumulative number of continuations or pre-standard CONs to balance prosecution histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes: continuation filings and child applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcomes are (i) probability of filing a continuation (CON) and (ii) probability of filing any child application (including continuations-in-part, divisionals, and reissues). Outcomes are often reported as CON × 100 or Child × 100 (percentage points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child applications are considered as broader outcomes since they capture other strategic filings; separate analyses examine CONs specifically and 'child' more broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office actions considered and statistics reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on three office actions: the first non-final rejection, the first final rejection, and the first notice of allowance. For each office action report (i) percentage of applications that receive the office action, (ii) conditional probability of filing the first continuation within six months from the date of the office action, and (iii) conditional probability that the first continuation is filed within six months from the date of the office action (conditional on generating a continuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statistics are reported separately for SEPs and matched controls to assess differences in prosecution responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month window for measuring continuations after office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure filings within a six-month window after an office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified because applicants have three months to reply to a rejection and can obtain up to three more months by paying a fee; failure to reply within this period implies abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures of patent scope change
rubrics_metrics.description: Two measures of patent scope change from published application to granted patent: (i) change in the number of independent claims (Marco et al., 2019), and (ii) change in the length of the first independent claim (Kuhn and Thompson, 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are used to test whether claim narrowing/expansion is correlated with continuation filing, via linear probability models controlling for filing year, issue year, art unit, and examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation criterion for continuations' purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret continuation filings in light of whether they respond to rejections or are used to obtain additional claims after allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results suggesting higher continuation probability after notice of allowance and modest relationship with rejections support the conclusion that continuations are primarily used to add new claims after allowance rather than to respond to rejections or claim narrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference-in-differences (DiD) baseline specification and fixed effects choices
rubrics_metrics.description: DiD regressions estimate PostStandard × SEP interaction effects using pooled cross-section OLS (dependent variable CON × 100) with various fixed effects: quarter FE, age FE, art-unit-by-examiner-by-filing-quarter (AU-E-FQ) FE, application FE, and polynomial age controls (age2, age3 & age4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple specifications (pooled, tech & cohort fixed effects, application fixed effects) are reported to show robustness; standard errors clustered by application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control variables for application characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Include controls for number of independent claims, average length of independent claims, number of inventors, dummies for claiming priority to provisional and PCT applications, dummies for small entities, and dummies for claiming priority to foreign applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These observables partially capture invention scope, invention quality, and prior investments in prosecution to mitigate confounding between SEP status and propensity to file continuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation checks using leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Include four leads of an indicator equal to one for SEPs in the quarter of standard publication to capture anticipation effects of standard publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the assumption that standard publication is exogenous, positive pre-standard coefficients can indicate anticipation; results show relatively large anticipation effects in the quarter before standard publication but similar PostStandard × SEP coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piecewise constant hazard model as robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a piecewise constant hazard specification where the outcome is the probability of a first continuation conditional on not having prior continuations; remove an application after the first period any continuation is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat exercise using information on all child applications as an alternative outcome; consistent results across hazard and linear models strengthen robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-study estimators addressing staggered timing and heterogeneous effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ modern estimators to address problems in staggered DiD: (i) compute de Chaisemartin & D’Haultfœuille (2020b) weights for TWFE regressions and use their estimator, (ii) use Sun & Abraham (2020) estimator to avoid contamination across periods, (iii) use Callaway & Sant’Anna (2020) estimator to estimate group-time average treatment effects, and (iv) implement the Borusyak et al. (2021) imputation estimator (doubly robust approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computational constraints require using 1-to-1 matched samples or random subsamples for some estimators; reported results from these estimators are similar to main analysis and used as robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational handling and subsampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where full-sample estimation is computationally demanding, use 1-to-1 matched samples or random subsamples (e.g., two random subsamples of 500 matched SEP-control pairs) to implement computationally intensive estimators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows use of Callaway & Sant’Anna and similar estimators on manageable sample sizes while checking consistency with full-sample TWFE results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering and inference conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard errors are clustered by application; significance reported with conventional stars (*** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust standard errors are used in regressions; inference conventions are described alongside tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative sample and specification checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustness checks include: (i) defining SEPs narrowly (only declared SEPs in disclosure letters), (ii) using only granted patents, (iii) 1-to-1 matching on filing month and technology center, (iv) restricting sample to SEPs filed before standard publication, and (v) using SEPs linked to ETSI vs other SSOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These alternative samples produce results very similar to main specifications, bolstering robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of child application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Child applications include continuations, continuations-in-part, divisionals, and reissues; analysis sometimes focuses only on continuations and sometimes on all child types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These other child applications may be used strategically but are less frequent or used differently; including them yields similar results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic estimation window
rubrics_metrics.description: Dynamic/event-study analyses use a seventeen-quarter window centered around standard publication to estimate pre-trends and post-standard effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plots of dynamic effects (with 95% confidence intervals) from several estimators (Callaway & Sant’Anna, Sun & Abraham, Borusyak et al.) are used to visualize timing and magnitude of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for time-varying technology-area shocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Interact calendar quarter indicators with art-unit, art-unit-by-filing-quarter, or art-unit-by-filing-quarter-by-examiner effects to capture time-varying shocks affecting groups of similar technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interactions are included to ensure that observed PostStandard × SEP effects are not driven by differential time-varying shocks across technology areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO small entity definition as a covariate
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity defined as independent inventors, companies with less than 500 employees and non-profit organizations; used as a dummy control variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small entities receive fee discounts at USPTO; controlling for small-entity status captures differences in applicant resources and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of descriptive statistics and sample construction details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed summary statistics (means, SD, quartiles) for variables such as CON, CONs, PostStandard × SEP, SEP indicator, age, number of independent claims, words per independent claim, number of inventors, provisional/PCT flags, small entity, foreign priority, and leniency (grant rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear definition of units (application-quarter), sample period (filed on or after November 29, 2000), and matching/membership rules is required to interpret results and replicate analyses.
